quotes.quote: Blink reformats 14 classic computer vision tasks into 3,807 multiple-choice questions, paired with single or multiple images and visual prompting.
We carefully evaluate 17 multimodal LLMs with various sizes (i.e., 7B, 13B, 34B) on Blink.
In total, we contribute 3.9K multiple-choice questions and 7.3K images, with an even distribution between the validation and test sets.
To guarantee the quality of Blink, we manually go through all collected data and filter out data that are ambiguous.
we first generate synthetic images using Stable Diffusion XL [63], employing COCO captions [46] as prompts.
We follow standard setups as in the VLMEvalKit [22], where the temperature is set to 0 and retry is set to 10.
Even the most advanced models, GPT-4V and Gemini Pro and Claude 3 OPUS, achieve accuracies of only 51.26%, 45.72%, and 44.11% respectively.
On Blink, Caption + LLM fails, achieving random guessing performance.
Even the powerful GPT-4V and Gemini models only achieve around 50% accuracy on Blink, far below the 95.7% human performance.
Results of different models on the Blink test set.
Comparison between multimodal LLMs, specialists, and human performance on the Blink dev set.
There are three types of visual prompts in Blink: circles, boxes, and masks
we extract the choices using GPT-3.5 [13]
The human agreement scores range between 80-99%, with the lowest being on art style and functional correspondence, highest being relative depth, object localization, and forensics detection.
Total Questions 3,807
Total Images 7,358
Detailed statistics of the Blink benchmark.
We evaluate Blink on 16 various large multimodal LLMs.
Blink makes use of data from existing image datasets, and does not cover all the visual perception abilities in the wild.
